title: OSPF Authentication: The Complete Beginner's Guide

scenes.narration: By default, any router can join your O S P F network. Even one an attacker plugged in. Authentication makes routers prove who they are.

scenes.heading: The guarded conference room
scenes.narration: Think of a conference room with a guard at the door. Type zero means no guard at all. Type one is a password shouted out loud for anyone to hear. Type three uses a secret that is never spoken, only proven. Set it on each interface, or for a whole area.

scenes.heading: The commands
scenes.narration: Here's the cryptographic version. Turn on message digest mode on the interface. Then give it a key number and a secret. And check the neighbour list.

lines.note: Turn on MD5 on the interface

scenes.heading: Common mix-ups
scenes.narration: Three traps. Only type three hashes the key. You still need keys on each interface. A mismatch leaves the neighbour stuck before full.

items.wrong: A failure drops the neighbour to DOWN
items.right: It sticks at INIT or EXSTART

scenes.heading: Remember this
scenes.cta: Try the Courseiva OSPF authentication lab
scenes.narration: So, to recap. Type three uses an M D five hash, and type one is plaintext. Both ends need the same key. A mismatch leaves neighbours stuck. Ready to practise? Try the Courseiva OSPF authentication lab.
